themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked dramatically to 23 this week compared to a 2.0-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1050% increase (z-score: 14.85)—suggesting a sudden surge in Uber/Lyft activity, illegal pickups, or traffic violations in Washington Heights/Inwood that emerged THIS WEEK.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0-per-week baseline (z-score: 14.85, 1050% increase)
Statistically anomalous spike with highest z-score among all detected deviations
No prior context available; suggests abrupt operational or behavioral change
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local business owners about increased for-hire vehicle congestion and illegal pickups on neighborhood streets
Contact TLC to determine if there's been a recent policy change, surge pricing event, or influx of new drivers licensed to operate in CD 112

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampment Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 13 last week versus a 1.0-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 1200% surge (z-score: 10.73)—indicating a rapid escalation in visible homelessness in parks and public spaces that emerged LAST WEEK.
evidence: 13 encampment complaints last week vs. 1.0-per-week average (z-score: 10.73, 1200% increase)
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite 'enhance park safety through more security staff' as unfunded priority
Spike aligns with seasonal winter shelter demand and potential closure or capacity constraints at local facilities
reporting_angles: Identify specific parks or public spaces where encampments have appeared; photograph and map locations
Interview NYC Department of Homeless Services and local shelter operators about capacity, recent policy changes, or intake freezes
Profile affected residents in encampments to understand why they are unsheltered and what services they need

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.1-per-week baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—pointing to rapid tree degradation or storm damage across the district that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1-per-week baseline (z-score: 8.69, 2300% increase)
Community Board budget requests cite 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' as recurring unfunded need
Suggests potential recent weather event, disease outbreak, or deferred maintenance crisis in neighborhood canopy
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine if there was a recent storm, pest outbreak (e.g., spotted lanternfly, emerald ash borer), or disease affecting street trees
Document specific dead or dying trees across the district; assess whether this reflects broader canopy health concerns in CD 112
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance budgets and replanting timelines in Washington Heights/Inwood

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Violation of park rules complaints increased to 4 last week from a 0.6-per-week average—a 540% spike (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting new disruptive activity or reduced park enforcement in neighborhood green spaces LAST WEEK.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints last week vs. 0.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.85, 540% increase)
Coincides with encampment spike, suggesting potential overlap between homelessness and park misuse complaints
Community Board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety and security staff funding
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are receiving the most rule-violation complaints; interview Parks Enforcement Patrol about staffing levels
Talk to regular park users about what specific violations they've observed (drinking, drug use, aggression, etc.)
Determine if encampment activity is driving or correlated with rule-violation complaints

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Complaint Decline
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints dropped 52% to 49 THIS WEEK from a 102.4-per-week average (z-score: -4.44)—a significant decline that may reflect seasonal patterns, contractor backlog resolution, or reporting lag, but warrants verification to rule out under-reporting.
evidence: 49 plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 102.4-per-week average (z-score: -4.44, 52% decrease)
Contradicts long-running heat/hot water crisis (8,931 complaints over 90 days), suggesting possible data reporting artifact
Requires verification that complaints are being logged accurately and not delayed
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to confirm whether plumbing repair backlogs have cleared or if 311 reporting is experiencing a lag
Cross-check with landlord repair data to verify that plumbing issues are genuinely declining or if residents have stopped calling 311
